title: Maximum Candies You Can Get from Boxes
summary: You possess n boxes numbered from 0 to n-1.
statement: You possess n boxes numbered from 0 to n-1. Each box has a status (open or closed), a count of candies, a list of keys that unlock other boxes, and a list of contained boxes. You start with a set of initial boxes. You can open boxes, collect their candies, use their keys to open more boxes, and access the contents of those boxes. The task is to determine the greatest number of candies you can collect by following these rules.
constraints: All five inputs describe the same n boxes; status one means initially unlocked.
You may open only a box you possess and have unlocked, then gain its candy, keys, and contained boxes.
Open each box at most once and return the maximum collectible candy total.
hints: A box becomes usable only when both owned and unlocked.
Track owned, unlocked, and already-opened sets separately.
Queue each newly usable box; opening it may add keys and boxes that make more boxes usable.
Every legal opening is eventually queued, and processing a box once collects its candy exactly once.
editorial: Maintain the two independent permissions—possession and an unlocked status—and their intersection is the frontier. Opening a frontier box grows both sets and may expose more frontier boxes. A processed set prevents duplicate candy. The independent oracle repeatedly scans the entire intersection to a fixed point rather than using event-driven queue updates.

tests.explanation: Opening zero reveals two; two supplies the key to one, for seven plus four plus five candy.
Both initially owned open boxes contribute, totaling ten.
